title: Bound async preview work and define generated Unity-object ownership
description:
## User Mandate

> "Sythesize these into durable tasks. Ensure nothing is lost. We're trying to emphasize consolidation, deduping, decomposition of god classes, and other codebase health improvements"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Preserve every accepted mechanism from the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03 audits in a durable owner or explicit rejected/unresolved record.
- Consolidate overlapping async preview, stale-result, generated-object lifetime, and editor decomposition work instead of creating parallel task families.
- Preserve deterministic synchronous fallback behavior and authoritative DNA ownership.

## Summary

Harden the asynchronous preview boundary after the first scheduler/controller slice. Bound stale work, remove double definition capture, carry request-scoped diagnostics, and define ownership and domain-reload behavior for generated Unity preview objects.

## Scope

- Make latest-request-wins bound queued work with one running request and at most one queued request, or an equivalent measured policy.
- Choose one owner for detached definition capture. The scheduler and preview controller must not both clone the same request.
- Carry sequence, revision, validation summary, failed stage, and failure classification with the generation result.
- Distinguish current, superseded, disposed, cancelled, domain, infrastructure, and unexpected completion states with a minimal contract.
- Make the preview controller the explicit owner of generated Mesh, MeshCollider, GameObject, and child preview objects. Never destroy source assets.
- Define and test domain-reload policy, accepted-result identity, replacement cleanup, and late-result disposal.
- Keep CreatureEditorWindow as coordinator and route complete result application through the preview controller.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Repeated preview requests do not create unbounded queued work, and superseded work is not started when it is already known stale.
- A request captures the definition exactly once and the synchronous Generate path remains a deterministic reference.
- Failure UI displays diagnostics captured for the failed request, never mutable validation state for a newer definition.
- Replacing or disposing a preview releases generated Unity objects without destroying source mesh/material assets.
- Domain reload follows one documented policy and leaves no stale accepted artifact or leaked generated object.
- Focused scheduler and editor tests cover coalescing, disposal, result identity, diagnostic correlation, replacement, and late completion. Unity SceneView smoke validation covers drag, cancellation, stale blocking, collider replacement, and domain reload.

## Validation

Run runtime/editor builds, focused scheduler tests, and the full available Unity EditMode/PlayMode suites. Perform the required Unity SceneView and domain-reload manual checks. Record queue depth, clone count, completion disposition, and generated-object cleanup evidence.

## Findings

Sources S05 and S06, F-12 through F-19 and F-36 through F-38: the scheduler starts every request and only suppresses stale application; PreviewController and scheduler both clone; result failure context is incomplete; generated Unity-object ownership and domain-reload policy are implicit; the controller remains a broad policy hub. TSK-0103 is correctly retained as the completed async foundation, not reopened for its validated parity slice. This follow-up owns the residual boundary work and coordinates with CC-094 and CC-052/061.

## Blockers

Unity execution is required for SceneView lifecycle, domain reload, and Unity-object destruction evidence. Do not mark Done from static inspection alone.

## Next Step

Define the request/result and ownership contracts, then add the smallest scheduler coalescing and preview cleanup tests before implementation.

comments.body: Council follow-up 2026-09-03: source traceability is S05/S06, docs/audits/creaturecreator-audit-synthesis-2026-09-03.md, Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/CreatureGenerationScheduler.cs, Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreaturePreviewController.cs, Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreatureEditorWindow.cs, and Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreaturePreviewAcceptanceState.cs. Add the third transient limb-drag clone to capture accounting. Result identity must match current DNA, and SceneView gates must cover each gesture owner, hot-control cleanup, preview root/Mesh disposal, collider replacement, late results, and domain reload. Bounded scheduler work may proceed in parallel; final identity/lifetime closure depends on CC-091 snapshot/revision contract.
